_comment: Deterministically-environment-red inventory (#781). A test whose law cannot hold in a known environment — the wal-shipper [G4] class, fixed as an instance in #782 — is neither a flake (tests/quarantine.json) nor merely a declared skip (tests/skips.json): quarantine would exclude it everywhere to silence one environment, and the skip budget records the hole without the environment shape or a revisit discipline. The mechanism is therefore a REQUIRED env guard (skipIf / runtime t.skip — which also lands in the skip budget) plus this ledger: every environment-predicate guard site (process.platform / process.arch / process.getuid comparisons in test files, discovered by scripts/test-report/env-red-inventory.mjs over the same globs as skip-inventory) must be recorded here with the guarded test, the human-readable predicate, the guard mechanism, an OPEN tracking issue, and an expiresAt date or a revisitTrigger sentence. An expired entry is a hard failure; _budget is DOWN-ONLY — the way to shrink this file is the #782 move: rewrite the test so the environment stops mattering. Keys are <path>#<ordinal>; `line` is informational and refreshed by `node scripts/test-report/env-red-inventory.mjs --write`.

packages/gateway/src/cli/service-install.environment: Red off darwin: the law drives real launchctl bootstrap/bootout, and no other platform has launchd to assert against.
packages/gateway/src/cli/service-install.revisitTrigger: Revisit if the service layer gains a systemd --user e2e rig — that would make the install/uninstall law assertable on linux runners (rig tracker: #790).

packages/gateway/src/cli/status-admin.te.environment: Red on win32: the status probe shells out to launchctl/systemctl, which exist only on darwin and linux; four tests share this predicate via skipIf.
packages/gateway/src/cli/status-admin.te.revisitTrigger: Revisit if the CLI grows a windows service adapter (sc.exe/SCM); until then win32 has no service surface for these four scenarios to assert (rig tracker: #790).

packages/vault/src/blob/disk-full.integr.test: FsBlobStore.putSync against a REAL full filesystem
packages/vault/src/blob/disk-full.integr.environment: Red off darwin: the real full-filesystem ENOSPC rig is built with hdiutil, which only darwin ships.
packages/vault/src/blob/disk-full.integr.revisitTrigger: Revisit if the nightly lane gains a linux loop-device/tmpfs ENOSPC rig — that would widen the environment where the real-disk law runs (rig tracker: #790).

packages/vault/src/wal-shipper-clone.tes.test: the base clone is a reflink
packages/vault/src/wal-shipper-clone.tes.environment: Red on ext4 runners: ext4 cannot reflink at all, so the cloning-consumes-no-new-disk assertion holds unconditionally only on APFS (darwin).
packages/vault/src/wal-shipper-clone.tes.revisitTrigger: Revisit if CI gains a btrfs/xfs runner where reflink holds — the guard could then narrow from platform to filesystem capability (rig tracker: #790).

tests/perf/vault-write.perf.test.ts#1.test: journalled vault writes stay within the nightly latency and fsync budget
tests/perf/vault-write.perf.test.ts#1.environment: The fsync-per-write count is countable only via strace on linux; off linux the test asserts latency alone rather than failing on an unmeasurable law.
tests/perf/vault-write.perf.test.ts#1.revisitTrigger: Revisit if a darwin syscall counter usable without SIP friction (dtrace) becomes available to the perf lane; then the fsync gate can widen (rig tracker: #790).

tests/perf/vault-write.perf.test.ts#2.test: journalled vault writes stay within the nightly latency and fsync budget
tests/perf/vault-write.perf.test.ts#2.environment: The inverse arm of site #1: in linux CI, where strace is provisioned by e2e.yml, a missing strace throws rather than skipping the fsync gate into a false green.
tests/perf/vault-write.perf.test.ts#2.revisitTrigger: Stands as long as the nightly perf lane installs strace (.github/workflows/e2e.yml); revisit together with site #1 (rig tracker: #790).
